ghosts.name: Laser Mirror
ghosts.job: Placed by the Apollo 11 crew as a target for lasers fired from Earth, to measure exactly how far away the Moon is.
ghosts.reply: SIGNAL RETURNED. LIGHT MADE THE ROUND TRIP IN 2.5 SECONDS.
ghosts.story: I'm a tray of 100 tiny mirrors. Scientists on Earth still aim lasers at me, and I bounce the light right back.
qs: How can a mirror still work?
It needs no power at all. It just sits there and bounces light back, like a bike reflector.
What did scientists learn?
The Moon is drifting away from Earth, about 3.8 cm every year. That's about how fast your fingernails grow.

ghosts.name: Eagle's Launch Pad
ghosts.job: Apollo 11's lander. It carried the first two people down to the Moon's surface in July 1969.
ghosts.story: Half of me stayed behind. When the astronauts blasted off, my top half flew back to their ship. My legs are still standing in the dust.
qs: Why leave it there?
The bottom half was the launch pad. Leaving it behind made the trip home lighter.
Can anyone see it now?
Yes! NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter has photographed the landing site from above.
ghosts.photoAlt: The Apollo 11 lunar module Eagle in lunar orbit, July 1969

ghosts.name: Surveyor 3
ghosts.job: A robot lander sent to prove a spacecraft could land softly, and to dig into the soil before astronauts came.
ghosts.story: I landed here alone. Two years later, two astronauts walked over to visit and took my camera home to Earth.
qs: Why did astronauts visit?
To see what years on the Moon do to a machine. They brought parts home to study.
Is it still there?
Yes, minus the camera and a few parts the astronauts took home.
ghosts.photoAlt: Surveyor 3 on the Moon, photographed by the Apollo 12 crew

ghosts.name: Moonquake Station
ghosts.job: A set of science instruments left by Apollo 12 to measure moonquakes, magnetism, and the solar wind.
ghosts.story: I listened to the Moon. I felt moonquakes and space rocks hitting the ground, and I radioed it all home for years.
qs: What's a moonquake?
The Moon shakes too! Instruments like me felt moonquakes and meteorite hits.
Why was it turned off?
In 1977 NASA switched the stations off to save money for new missions.

ghosts.name: Apollo 15 Rover
ghosts.job: The first Moon car, brought by Apollo 15 so astronauts could explore much farther from their lander.
ghosts.story: I was the first car on the Moon. Two astronauts drove me over hills and craters, then parked me for good.
qs: Could I drive it?
Its batteries are dead, so it can't move now. Astronauts drove it about 28 km on the Moon.
Why bring a car?
To explore farther than walking allowed, and to carry rocks and tools.

ghosts.name: Apollo 17 Rover
ghosts.job: Carried the last Apollo crew across the Taurus-Littrow valley to collect rocks and samples.
ghosts.story: I was driven on the very last Apollo trip. After my astronauts left, I've been parked in this valley ever since.
qs: How far did it go?
About 36 km, the farthest any Apollo rover drove.
Who drove it last?
The Apollo 17 crew, in December 1972. Nobody has driven on the Moon since.
